Subject: Reference request: Redwood evaluation at OptiCloud

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well. We wrapped our internal evaluation of Redwood last quarter and the platform made a big difference for our AI feature throughput — the execs are excited. We wanted to check whether someone from OptiCloud could be a short reference for Redwood: a 20–30 minute call and permission to use a short quote in a case study.

Our team (product + procurement) are available next week. I can loop in procurement if you need an MSA/contract contact. Happy to sign any reasonable quote approvals.

Thanks,
Emilia

Hi Emilia — great to hear, and thank you for the kind words. We’d love to feature OptiCloud. Before we schedule anything, I want to confirm one thing internally: I’m aware of a recent production incident OptiCloud reported in late Jan and I want to be sensitive about the timing if the customer is still in renewal or mitigation. Can our team check whether this would be ok from a customer-success and legal perspective?

If you’re comfortable, could you share a short timeline of the incident or point me to the case notes (we’ll keep it confidential)? We can also delay publication until after your renewal window if that’s better.

I’ll loop in our CS and legal so we don’t do anything that could cause friction.

Best,

Marissa — reading through the renewal notes and CS logs: OptiCloud did experience a degraded region failover on 2026-01-24 which triggered expanded support involvement. The customer accepted a credit and we opened a postmortem; they are currently in a 60-day mitigation follow-up with our SRE team.

Recommendation: Pause any public-facing reference or case study until we confirm that the mitigation window closed and the account is stable — especially because OptiCloud’s execs raised questions during renewal. If we proceed, we should avoid quoting SLA numbers or callouts to specific uptime improvements until after we have final postmortem signoff.

I’ve attached a redacted incident timeline we prepared for internal review (OptiCloud_incident_timeline.xlsx) and a one-page case notes summary (OptiCloud_case_summary.pdf). These are for internal assessment only.

-Rishi
Customer Success Manager

Team — legal view: we should not publish until we have: (1) explicit written approval from OptiCloud’s legal/procurement for the quote and the case study language; (2) confirmation that the customer does not consider the incident an ongoing escalation; and (3) redaction of any sensitive operational details.

If OptiCloud wants to proceed now, we can offer an anonymized case study (no company name, industry-only language) or a customer-approved quote limited to product value without incident metrics. I attached our standard redaction guidelines and quote approval checklist (reference_redaction_guidelines.docx).

If procurement is involved, we should expect a short review cycle and possibly a redline to the quote.

-Monica
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Reference request: Redwood evaluation at OptiCloud

Hi Emilia — thanks for reaching out and for the quick reply earlier. I checked in with our CS and legal teams and we want to be cautious here given the Jan incident and your ongoing mitigation window. Two quick options:

1) Short delay: we can schedule the 20–30 minute reference call now but mark it as an internal sales reference only (no public quote or case study) until we receive procurement/legal signoff from OptiCloud.

2) Anonymized quote: OptiCloud can approve a brief, anonymized quote that avoids mentioning incident timing, SLAs, or region-specific performance. We’ll provide suggested language and a fast approval path.

If you’d like us to wait until after your renewal closes, that’s also fine — we want to avoid any perception of pressuring during mitigation. Please let me know which path you prefer and whether procurement should be looped in now.

Thanks again — we appreciate the partnership and want to make sure any public story is comfortable for your team.

Warmly,
Marissa
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
